headline: Executive order makes 2023 updates to the Manual for Courts-Martial, the rulebook for military criminal trials.
what_it_does: This order changes the Manual for Courts-Martial, the official guide for how the U.S. military investigates, charges, tries, and sentences service members accused of crimes. Presidents update this manual from time to time by executive order. The title does not list the specific changes, so the exact details are not covered here.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the U.S. armed forces
who_it_affects.how: Service members accused of crimes under military law would face trials and sentences under the updated rules.

who_it_affects.group: Military judges, prosecutors, and defense lawyers
who_it_affects.how: They must follow the revised procedures when handling courts-martial.

who_it_affects.group: Victims and witnesses in military criminal cases
who_it_affects.how: Their part in military trials may be shaped by the updated rules, though the specific changes are not stated in the title.

when_it_takes_effect: Not stated in the provided material; the order was signed July 28, 2023.
